utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic, Dragan Jokic, and Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, shall we continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Your Honour, prior to the witness arriving, there were a couple of points I wanted to make with regard to the video and the portions that you are about to see today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: We have provided to the Court a -- and to the Defence an identity book that corresponds to this particular video which has the names and the identities of the different individuals that are depicted on the video, and that can be used as a reference after the fact to identify people that may appear on video rather briefly. I would, however, like to point out as a point of reference, because it is something that future witnesses will testify concerning, that in this second Hotel Fontana meeting, there is a -- and you will hear a pig squealing in the background, and the witnesses who will testify subsequently will make reference to that particular event, and so I wanted to call that to the Court's attention. Additionally, present at the second Hotel Fontana meeting is General Krstic, who you will see seated next to General Mladic, as well as Kostric [phoen], who is the Drina Corps intelligence officer and Momir Nikolic, who is present but not on the camera. Nesib Mandzic, also a witness who will testify shortly before Your Honours is present on camera. And then with regard to the third Hotel Fontana meeting which follows on the video after the second, you will see Momir Nikolic standing out in front of the Hotel Fontana with Radislav Jankovic and Vujadin Popovic, as well as General Mladic and General Krstic at the meeting, which also included Vojodin Popovic, and Miroslav Deronjic, who was the civilian representative appointed by Radovan Karadzic, the three Muslim representatives as well as the Dutch. So I wanted to clarify that for the Court because I understand that the witness has the ability to stop the video. However, we would like to allow it to play in its entirety as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour. What we just heard was a summary. Now, I understand that the Prosecutor was trying to be helpful to the Court. But I would appreciate if the evidence comes through the witness rather than the Prosecutor, otherwise we need to have the Prosecutor sworn as a witness so she can testify. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. In this respect I agree with you. But anyway, let's have that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Before that, could you tell me what's in your hands, what's in that bundle, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This binder is the binder of the exhibits that will be presented during my testimony, as well as the outline of questions that will be forwarded to me by the Prosecutor. I have in addition to that one document that summarises body counts in various mass graves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Ms. De la Torre.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We will proceed now with the continuation of the video which begins with the second Hotel Fontana meeting on the 11th of July, 1995. We will give the witness a mouse, which will allow him the ability to stop the video if he has a comment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to mention that the noise that is heard on the video is a scream of a pig that is being slaughtered nearby. You will have recognised General Krstic, commander -- deputy commander of the Drina Corps that day. So arrival of civilian representatives. The first person is Camila Omanovic and the man behind is Ibro Nuhanovic. In addition to the persons who were present at the previous meeting, here are more people. They are civilian representatives of the municipality of Bratunac, that I will pinpoint a bit later. You have also a representative of the police, General Vasic. You also can see at the -- at the right of the screen Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, Drina Corps security officer. You also have -- I don't remember his name, the one which has the moustache with the intelligence -- of the corps. I don't remember. Sorry. And you have also at the right of this table Mr. Miroslav Deronjic, the president of the SDS for the area of Bratunac. This is a group of men that was detained in the White House and was walking towards specific buses to be transported to Bratunac. Here they are walking on the opposite side of the road than the other refugees are walking on, and in between the buses are soldiers who prevent them to board these buses or trucks. All these bags are the belongings of the men who were separated and then taken to the White House that is just behind. These are the men sitting on the balcony of the White House. This is the last stage of the evacuation of the people. This is the moment where those who were inside the UN base are requested to board the buses and to follow the deportation route.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the Court is agreeable, this might be a good time to take a break. We are done with the Potocari section, before we move on to the next topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We are adjourned until twenty to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to apologise. We're using a new video system here for this video, and we realise that there was an approximately 20-minute section of Potocari that was missing. The video was prepared sequentially, so this would be a bit out of order. However, we would like to go ahead and -- and play it now, go back and pick it up. The last section of the video where we left off leaves Potocari and moves on along the road. We would like to reserve that and play that on Monday, once we're able to get some of the kinks out. Once we finish with the Potocari section, we can go on with Mr. Ruez's testimony and deal with the rest of the video on Monday, if that's acceptable to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is exactly where the separation line was, 12th July, just at the exit of the Express compound.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that concludes the Potocari section of the video in its entirety. So we'd like to leave it here for today and go back to the questioning of Mr. Ruez, picking up the video on Monday, with the last segment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, having finished --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we have some technical problems here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Leaving the video for the time being, Mr. Ruez, I'd like to go to an overview of the crime scenes you identified during the course of your investigation. Referring to Prosecution Exhibit 16.1, you mentioned in your testimony yesterday that the women and children were being deported from Potocari to a location you identified as Kladanj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, in the video there is a segment called" "Luke to Kladanj." Using Prosecution Exhibit 16.1, can you indicate for the Court geographically the significance of -- of Kladanj and Luke, where they are vis-a-vis the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But we don't have the relevant exhibit, I think, on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: I'm just going to refer you, Mr. Ruez, back to Prosecution Exhibit 24, which is the large map of the entire area.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So Kladanj is at -- at the west of this map. Kladanj is a town that is on the so-called at that time Muslim-held territory. So just after the confrontation line that was separating Republika Srpska territory and Bosniak territory. We could see on the video that this area is an area of a canyon with a little river flowing in the middle, and they are a series -- there is a series of tunnels that -- through which the people went through to reach the town of Kladanj. Just before the area where the people were dropped off the buses and the trucks is a little elementary school called the Luke School. And after having got out of the buses, the men who were still together with their families at that point were separated and taken towards that school, which is approximately 400 metres towards the west -- sorry, towards the east of the dropping spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And approximately how far is Luke from Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 4 or 5 kilometres, and Luke is approximately very roughly 40 kilometres by road from Bratunac or from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Thank you. We're finished with this map. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, when did you first identify Luke as a potential crime scene?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luke was identified as a possible crime scene following the interview of one witness who was on-board of a bus. I think it was 13 July, arrived in Luke, he went through this separation process, was taken to this elementary school, where he stayed for the afternoon. On a meadow first, then was taken inside the little building. I think we have this exhibit coming on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Referring to Prosecution Exhibit 4.1, were you able to locate the building or the school that the survivor indicated he was held in?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we could do so only after having taken this man on the spot with us, because prior that we couldn't figure out that this tiny building so close to the confrontation line was the one. But ultimately this witness went with us and pinpointed that elementary school as being the detention site for him.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Moving on to Prosecution Exhibit 4.2. Did the witness indicate where in the school he was held?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are two classrooms in this school, and he was taken inside this one. He pinpointed the location where he was sitting, together with approximately 15 people, and how they went also through a beating process in this classroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Where were the prisoners taken from the school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of the -- of that day, this man was -- who testified here during the trial of General Krstic, and we have the records of this, was taken on-board of a little truck, was driven towards Vlasenica town, which is approximately 10 kilometres to the east of Luke. He recognised some lamps which are along the side of the road in front of Vlasenica, then recognised also that the truck was turning nearby a football pitch, which is a football stadium in front of Vlasenica town, and from there he drove for an unknown time and distance, in fact, towards an area of hills that is north of Vlasenica, and at one point the truck stopped and he used the opportunity to jump off the truck and run away, was shot at but was missed, and would hear intense shooting happening behind him and made the assumption that this was the execution of the other prisoners who were on-board the truck with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Were you able to follow the route of this particular witness to verify his account of what had occurred?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We attempted to locate the execution site, but since the event happened during the night he was not able to spot precisely where this thing might have happened. I also --

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also have to add that since we have discovered many execution sites and mass grave sites through aerial imagery, unfortunately in this instance aerial imagery was not of use.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Moving on to Prosecution Exhibit 4.3. You have a map in which you have marked "Execution sites, main concentration site, and mass grave." Can you explain to the Court how it is that you marked this particular map?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this area, which is the zone where most of the people who were trapped in the woods and who surrendered on 13 July 1995 were assembled on some collection points first. And the final destination of these prisoners ultimately ended up being Bratunac town. They were then ultimately transported towards Bratunac town. But for a fraction of them, an unknown fraction of them, their immediate fate after having been captured or after having surrendered was to be taken towards execution sites, and these ones are marked here and will be developed then one by one. The reason of marking this map is also to show that every incident is separate but there is a pattern here during the day of 13 July that to me seems to indicate that there was an initial intent to deal with these prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to this witness making conclusions at this point. We have not decided what his expertise is as an expert witness, and he's drawing his own conclusions. I think that's inappropriate and we object to him voicing his opinion and drawing his on collusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe the Prosecutor could establish some foundations of this information so that we could understand whether it's a conclusion or it is hearsay evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, during the course of your investigation and your interviews with survivors, both of executions as well as transportations and deportations to Bratunac, were you able to ascertain where each of these individuals was captured and subsequently held?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For each of them we could determine at what location that person was -- surrendered, and from there we could reconstruct the -- the trip that they made from that point, until the final stage where they reached an execution site.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: In general terms, were you able, in speaking with these individuals, to establish a form of a time line with regard to when executions occurred versus when the shipments to Bratunac occurred?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The -- in fact, the -- the general events is quite simple. 12th of July is the day where the deportation starts for all the people who are in Potocari. All these people are shipped towards Kladanj. Separations are starting that day. The men are taken to Bratunac town after having been stored for a while in Potocari the White House. The next day is the day when this process continues in Potocari, but in addition to that begins the process of capturing and surrendering of all those who tried to flee through the forest and could not manage to break through the Serb lines at the end of the day of the 12th. So the sake of this exhibit was in fact to pinpoint on one map the various events that happened in this area during the day of the 13th. I retrieved my personal conclusion because I bet that such a conclusion could be done by anyone else once the knowledge of these events is known. In addition to these crime scenes are also marked two hardware facilities which are two brigades. One site is the location of the 5th Engineer Unit that belongs to the Drina Corps, and one other unit is spotted also on this map, which is an element of the 65th Protection Regiment, which is a unit attached to the main staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Having in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to ask the witness if we can find out what the basis is for his identification of these locations. Does he have forensic evidence, or is it just a summary of hearsay witnesses that we don't know where the foundation came from? If it's just witness statements, could he just tell us what witnesses he bases this information on and whether they will appear here to testify and be cross-examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think part of the problem could be solved by the questions asked by the Prosecutor. I believe she will lead us step by step, and part of the issues could be solved during the cross-examination. And you have the full title to dig deep into this issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And Your Honour, just for clarity, we do intend to go through each of these crime scenes and establish how it is that they became a part of Mr. Ruez's investigation. We're still on the overview at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, taking the map that you created here, Exhibit 4.3, can you give the Judges an idea of the proximity of the military facilities you've identified, the execution sites, and the concentration sites to one another?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we lose quality on these exhibits once they appear on the screen, but this map has squares and each of these squares is 1 kilometre. But unfortunately we cannot really see this on the -- on the screen. So let's say that the distance between Kravica and Konjevic Polje here is I would guess 6 kilometres, and then from Konjevic Polje to Nova Kasaba it is 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Having spent a fairly significant amount of time in this particular area, Mr. Ruez, despite the fact that this map is blown up many, many times, do you consider this to be a fairly small concentrated area from Kravica to Konjevic Polje to Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: The fact that all of these sites that you've indicated, the execution sites, the concentration sites, and the mass graves, are located in such close proximity to one another, does that give you as an investigator any indication as to whether or not this was an organised plan that was -- that was carried out on the 12th, 13th, 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to have to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: It calls for speculation on the part of the investigator. He wasn't present, and he's trying to speculate whether the Serb army had an organised policy there. I don't believe he's qualified to speculate on that and draw a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I basically was going to make the same objection. At least, no foundation has been laid for him to be able to give this sort of an opinion at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, during this trial, we are only going to hear the facts. Any conclusions will be drawn by this Bench. And if there are any more facts that the Prosecution would like to ask, you may proceed, but do not ask the witness to give some speculations or conclusions on those facts.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you had indicated yesterday that there was a particular significance of the location of Nova Kasaba and Konjevic Polje and Sandici vis-a-vis the trek of the column. Can you explain to the Court the relationship between the trek of the column and the sites that you have indicated as concentration sites on this particular map.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I already explained that on a previous exhibit that was showing both the trek of the column and the blockade of the Bosnian Serb forces. The surrender spots are in fact determined by the nature of the terrain in this area. The people were funneled towards this -- this intersection of Konjevic Polje, and as I said, those who were on this -- on this part of the terrain, on a huge hill, these ones were surrendering in between Konjevic Polje and Nova Kasaba. All those who were more towards the east were going down towards the asphalt road in the area of Sandici. And whatever meadow they were taken to initially, they were then re-grouped on the Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And I guess that's my point, Mr. Ruez. Does this map reflect your testimony yesterday with regard to how the column became trapped behind the line and were ultimately assembled as prisoners to be taken to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 5.2, can you explain to the Judges what this depicts?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The black dot that was marking the location of the 65th Protection Regiment near -- at Nova Kasaba - sorry - this photograph shows, in fact, the building as seen from the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And what is the significance of the 65th Protection Regiment?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the first significance is that it was located at that place, and for the rest it is a unit attached to the main staff. It is a unit designed to protect General Mladic and the facilities of the main staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 5.3. Can you explain to the Judges what this aerial image depicts?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I indicated previously, this compound to the 65th Protection Regiment was used to keep some prisoners which were UN prisoners. But these -- this UN personnel who was kept in this building could also testify about the fact that there were Muslim prisoners kept in this building as well. This photograph dated 13 July at 1400 hours shows the compound, which is at the bottom of the picture. And in front of this compound is a yard, and one can see that there are three buses on this yard. I would not be able to tell you if these buses are bringing prisoners or are coming to collect prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: When you indicate "UN prisoners," Mr. Ruez, who specifically are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to the members of the Dutch Battalion who were escorting the convoys towards Kladanj and who were stopped at checkpoints, who were taken in custody to this facility and had their vehicles taken away from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 5.4, can you explain to the Court the significance of the football pitch that's depicted in the middle right-hand section of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph shows an aerial view of the football pitch of Nova Kasaba and also the vicinity of Nova Kasaba town that starts just, in fact, when entering town, the first location one hits is this football pitch and then is the town. The compound we saw previously is at the exit of this town. This is going south.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: With regard to your investigation, what is the significance of this particular football field?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the main -- this is the main concentration spot for the prisoners who were captured in this area. And when I say "the area," it is in fact the area in between the intersection of Konjevic Polje and this football field. The people naturally avoided getting too close to Nova Kasaba. This is why they surrendered generally closer to the intersection than to Nova Kasaba town. But then they were brought to this football field, which is a convenient location to keep control of prisoners who are on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 3.5, can you in fact see the groups of prisoners who were collected on that field in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On this aerial photograph dated 13 July, 1400 hours, one can see the same football field as the one shown previously but through another angle. This is aerial imagery. And the -- the dark things that can be seen on this football field and who are -- who have a yellow circle around -- around them are groups of prisoners lined on rows -- lined in rows, sorry. It is impossible to assess how many people we are seeing on this photograph. And again, it is an instant shot, so it doesn't mean -- it does not mean that this is the entire amount of prisoners captured that day. It's only the amount of people who were present on this field at that specific timing.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, during the course of your investigation, were you able to ascertain whether or not General Mladic visited this particular site on this particular day?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Witnesses referred to the arrival of Mladic, who made a short stop at this soccer field and addressed the crowd, giving them a speech, and then left the place.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: The prisoners who were collected on this field during the course of the day, where were they taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as we know, since this is the -- the fate of at least one of the persons who -- who survived ultimately, he was taken with other prisoners who were on this field, put onboard of a vehicle, and they were driven to Bratunac town, where they stayed in a column of convoys -- in a convoy of buss and trucks.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: So am I correct in saying at this point, Mr. Ruez, you have the prisoners separated in Potocari now being held in Bratunac, as well as the groups of prisoners who were captured at Nova Kasaba, being bussed and held in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of the day of 13 July, 1995, all of the prisoners who survived the day of 13 July 1995 were all taken to Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: In the area of this particular football field, Mr. Ruez, were you able to identify execution sites as well as this particular holding site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 6.1, based upon witness accounts, were you able to locate an execution site in the area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This --

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: -- to object until he clarifies what witnesses and if they will appear to testify. He cannot summarise their testimony and come to a conclusion where the execution spots were located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe Ms. De la Torre will ask some questions to clarify this issue. Are there any witnesses to testify to this effect?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Our intent at this point is, with regard to these execution sites, is to discuss his investigation and how he was able to take information he received, go out to the scene, and verify the facts that had been relayed to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Ask some questions whether this witness has been to this particular spot and there was an investigation in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, just as an overview, the crime scenes that we are going to go through today and possibly Monday, have you visited all of them?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And were you present when the investigation was conducted to the point where evidence was collected and found based upon witness accounts that had been given to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on all of them during the entire time that type of work was conducted. And on this specific one, for example, it is an investigator from the team, assisted by Dean Manning who did the survey of a meadow and could find the elements that were confirming the declaration of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: So with regard to the particular crime scenes that we go through, can you clarify as we go through them which sites that you were present on while the investigation was conducted.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will mention it each time we hit a site. This might be the only exception. I've been on this meadow. We've searched for -- tried to locate this meadow during four years. When we finally found it, it was the last one that we -- we probed, and I was leaving the area the day before we started that process. So on this specific one, I was not present when the metal fragments and the bullet fragments and the bullets were found in the meadow that had been indicated as an execution spot by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Subsequent to the discovery of the evidence that was recovered at this particular location, were you able to review all of that evidence and compare what was recovered to the witness's account that had been given previously concerning the execution?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: For sure I reviewed all the material that was taken -- I mean, that was -- I mean, all the information that was provided to me after this mission was over by the investigator who -- who did the operation, and he produced also a document that maybe can be introduced in the courtroom about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: With -- as an investigator, with regard to the evidence that was recovered, did that evidence corroborate the witness account that had been given concerning this particular execution?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it essentially confirmed is that on the specific location that was -- on which the witness declared having seen the event that he -- he testified about not in court but to us, the only area where we could match -- we'd discover elements that were matching what he said was on the specific location that he had indicated, not 50 metres right, 100 metres right, or 200 metres left. It was a very specific concentration of bullets and bullet fragments on an approximately 15-metre by 20-large zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, what's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe that the witness just verified, one, that he's not really competent to testify about this site right here because he was not present. He didn't conduct the investigation. And two, he did just say that he was talking to a witness who verified that but the witness is not going to testify. And I think that that's the crux of that Milosevic decision. It's okay if he summarises witness testimony if the witness will be available to testify for cross-examination. But if it's evidence that the Prosecution is not putting forward, then it should not be allowed to be summarised in this hearsay on top of hearsay form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, of course we'll regard this piece of evidence as hearsay evidence. I think the issue is how much weight we should attach to this piece of the evidence. We'll hear what the witness is going to tell us. Yes, you may proceed, Ms. De la Torre.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you had indicated that it took approximately four years of investigation to locate this particular site. Do you recall when it was that you were finally able to identify this location?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the end of 1999. And the first attempt was in April 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court the information that you had that ultimately led you to identify this particular site as a potential crime scene.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That particular witness explained that meanwhile he was trying to find a way to cross the asphalt road and was overlooking the road, he was standing nearby an electrical pylon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I really apologise to the Court, but all my objection is is that if he's going to say what a witness said could we just know whether the witness is coming to testify in the case or whether he is a witness that they've just used to come to some summary conclusion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could you provide us with that kind of information?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In this particular case, the Prosecution did not intend to call this particular witness. However, this evidence is not being offered -- while it is hearsay in one respect, it is also not being offered for the truth of the matter asserted in that we are simply trying to detail for the Court the course of Mr. Ruez's investigation. If a witness says, "I happened to see this while I was walking through blood crossing a road," it's irrelevant whether or not that was in fact when or how he saw it. The point is based on that information, Mr. Ruez ended up at a particular site and once he arrived there he uncovered a crime scene. So I don't believe that the situation in Milosevic applies here, in that we are not attempting to introduce this evidence in lieu of the witness testimony. We're simply trying to detail Mr. Ruez's identification of different crime scenes, how he arrived at the scene in the first place, and what he found when he got there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have no objection if the witness comes to testify. But this is -- goes directly to one of the counts in the indictment, as to whether this happened or not, especially under the theory of joint criminal enterprise. And I believe that there's no problem with this line of questioning, as long as that witness will appear for cross-examination. If he is not being called by the Prosecution, then it violates the appellate ruling in Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll take into consideration your objections. Here we just want to know what the witness's personal knowledge of this crime scene. I hope that both parties will bear in mind about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I also just want to bring to the Honourable Trial Chamber's attention that he did say that he didn't do this investigation at this site; it was somebody else. So I don't know if he's competent to testify about what he personally knew at this scene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let me hear what will follow after his statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, can you explain briefly how it was that you were able to identify this particular location as a crime scene.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So as I said, the witness was standing nearby an electrical pylon, and he said that he saw in between two houses groups of prisoners being led. He could not ascertain the numbers of these prisoners. They were put to stand on a meadow, and parked in front of this meadow were three armoured vehicles, one UN APC, and two personnel transport carriers on tracks. On top of these vehicles were Serb soldiers who, when the people were lined up, started shooting on this group. According to the witness, this -- this situation occurred in three instances. After the third event, he left the area. What took in fact so much time to identify the spot is that there were several locations in between Konjevic Polje and this area, where from the pylon one could see things in between two houses. So we first checked all these other locations from north to south before we ultimately found this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I was trying to be very collegial and professional in bringing the Milosevic decision to the Prosecution's attention three days ago hoping that they would read it and re-read and it read it carefully. Obviously the lady Prosecutor has failed to read it carefully enough to understand that this sort of testimony goes specifically against the Milosevic decision. What I'm uncertain at this point is whether this particular witness has indeed questioned the witness upon which he's testifying to or is it a statement that he's read that was generated through a questioning process from somebody else from OTP or some other investigator. And I join in with Ms. Sinatra's objection, and I would ask the -- the Court to please ask the Prosecutor to lay a foundation, because now he is testifying and the information that's coming out is going more than -- than merely as to what a witness said. It appears that they are bringing it in for the truth of the matter asserted therein, which is -- and I understand hearsay can come in and it goes to the weight, but here we have a witness testifying about what another witness said and also about that witness's state of mind and as to why he was unable to find the location and so on and so forth. So maybe there is a good-faith basis for this witness being able to provide this testimony. But until we have a clear foundation - and this is sort of basic, elementary, you know, adversarial trial skills - until that, Your Honour, it would cause us to have some anxiety. It causes me to rise up and interfere and disrupt the proceedings, which I don't like to do unless I have to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that Madam Prosecutor is going to lay the foundations for this piece of the evidence step by step. Let us hear what kind of questions the Prosecutor will ask to this witness, especially concerning the foundations. The problem is that we should distinguish very clearly what is this witness heard and what he saw when he visited that place so that we could know how much weight we should attach to this piece of the evidence. Yes, you may proceed, Madam Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I think you were in the process of detailing for the Court how it was that you took this information and corroborated it, using the locations at this particular site. You first mentioned that the witness had indicated there was an electrical pylon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a witness with who I talked several hours and took an interview from him in 1996. After that interview, we had access to the area and tried by ourselves to pinpoint this location. We were unsuccessful. We returned to talk with this witness, and ultimately managed to convince him to come with us, to Republika Srpska, and to try to find this place together with him. He agreed to come. Unfortunately, he was so scared when we arrived on the spot that -- in this area that he never dared to step out of the vehicle. He was more or less lying on the back of the seat, not even daring showing his face, and arrived on the spot, and in this area when he saw the first pylon, he said, "Yes, this is probably the pylon." Unfortunately, the angle of what one can see when he's on the road and the angle seen when one is on the hill is very different, and he just dropped a location like this. This is why it took us so long, in fact, to find without his assistance the same elements that he was talking about to us but in another location, which was in fact 2 kilometres away from where we stopped when we were with him. But the first time he had that ability, without getting out of the vehicle anyhow, to help us find this location.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Once you arrived at the location that's depicted in Prosecution Exhibit 6.1, what elements at that particular scene were you able to identify that corroborated the witness account?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So again here I will in fact explain the information that has been forwarded by Dean Manning, investigator Dean Manning, who is the one who produced forensic report on his findings on that particular meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Were you present when this location was first identified as -- as the potential crime scene that was in question with regard to this particular witness?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because as I explained in 1999, we were in fact conducting an investigation in the vicinity of this spot, and prior leaving I did request that we would make a search on this meadow which was -- that was the last area we did not check, and this -- we should do this meanwhile we are conducting this investigation. And I had left the area the day after that this meadow was indeed scanned with a metal detector and the -- a specific area identified as a potential execution site that matched the description of the witness. In between two houses when looking towards the pylon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe it's clear for the Court to see now that Mr. Ruez was not present even at the time when he's talking about a witness who's lying in the back of the car, he wasn't there. He is testifying from something that is not admissible according to the appellant ruling in this case. And if it was admissible, I know the Court would determine what weight to give it to. But I think the first decision is whether it's admissible. And I don't believe that he should be allowed to testify on that line of questioning without telling us that he was present with the witness, number one, and that the witness is going to come testify here subject to cross-examination, number two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. As you said before, that we heard that the foundation is quite clear that the witness was not present at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But he's also testifying from some source about some witness saying that he was too afraid to get out of the car, and we don't know what source that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We should give an opportunity to the witness for him to explain to us. Yes, witness, do you have anything to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, definitely. The description I made of the behaviour of that witness, when we came on the spot, and, I'm the direct source of this because I was driving the vehicle. I was together with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I withdraw the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, based upon the interview you conducted with the witness and based upon the evidence at this particular location, have you been able personally to verify that the witness account detailed to you personally is corroborated by this particular -- the points of interest in this particular location?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because again, I know this terrain very well. I've spent hours walking in this area during several years. The reason why I believe this is very precisely the spot the witness is talking about is that, as you can see on the photograph - but it needs a little bit of imagination because of the question of sight -- angle of sight - the pylon we were referring to is at the left, top left of the picture. One can see a white line which is a path, in fact, a dirt track, but next to it is like -- is like a long. Yes. So here is -- there are two white lines. One is a path, and on the right is -- that's much too large. Left. Left. More, more, even more, much more, much more. Yes. Stop. For here, on this enlargement, at the left is a dirt track. But at the right it's an electrical pylon. You can eliminate this blow-up. And if you draw a line from that pylon towards the houses which are at the top of the picture above the asphalt road, you have, starting from the left, where there is this bend of the road that turns left, after that there are a few hills -- yes, perfect, towards the one. So that's the angle of sight that one has when being in the vicinity at the bottom of the pylon towards this direction. And the meadow on which we found the elements I will describe just after this, were found specifically on this area. I would add also that we have unfortunately an exhibit that we could have presented had we expected to enter these details, which is the map that Dean Manning generated to explain what was found precisely on this meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Could you describe, Mr. Ruez, what was discovered at that particular location, which is marked on Prosecution Exhibit 6.1 with a rectangle and the number "1" that corresponded to the witness account that had been given to you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We would have to go to the Exhibit 6.2, the following one. So this is a view of the meadow seen from the asphalt road. On -- on that meadow, you can see that there are white -- sorry, yellow little markers on the ground. These markers spot the position where metal fragments were found inside the ground, these metal fragments being bullets and bullet fragments and also some unidentified fragments. What was found also -- one has to remember that the -- the shooting was done according to the witness from people who were standing on top of APCs. That's also an important element because someone who would shoot from a low level at this ground, due to the terrain, most certainly the bullets would not go embedded in the soil. They would ricochet on such a slope. But due to the angle of firing from people who were on top of these vehicles, then the bullets penetrate the ground. And this is the reason why probably here we were able to find these concentrations of metal, which according to the size of the field where these fragments were found seems to match the description which was made by the witness at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, were you able to locate any grave sites that are in close proximity to this particular execution site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the vicinity of these sites are indeed mass grave sites.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Going back to Prosecution Exhibit 6.1. Could you explain to the Court what was found in the immediate vicinity of the execution site that you just detailed in Exhibit 6.2.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The areas on this photograph marked "A" and "B" mark the position of two mass grave sites, areas. In fact, one -- one mass grave and 1992 smaller graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 6.3, were you able to recover aerial images which correspond to the boxes which were indicated on Prosecution Exhibit 6.1?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This -- this photograph was part of those that were shown by Madeleine Albright to the United Nations in August 1995, and they show the presence of a disturbance in the area which is in the vicinity of a football field of Nova Kasaba. So on this particular picture, which is dated 27 July, there is a clear disturbance on several spots on this part of the terrain. What could not be seen on the previous picture, because it looked like woods, in fact there is a river just where the tree line was on the previous photograph, and these areas here also are protected from site when coming from the north thanks to these tree lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And for the sake of clarity, Mr. Ruez, when you refer to the aerial images of the crime scenes you identified and the fact that there is disturbed earth, could you explain to the Court the significance of that in the course of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we have a photograph, for example, dated 5 July of this area that shows no disturbance and then later on a photograph dated 27 July shows a disturbance, we always went to check the content of these areas which showed disturbance. Due to the knowledge of the events we had at that time, we could only suspect these places to be potential, possible mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Based upon the information you had received both from witnesses and from the aerial images, was this particular site probed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, in April 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 6.4, could you explain to the Court what you mean when you say that a site was "probed".

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We -- the word has two meanings. Sometimes when we say "we probed," is in fact to take a metal -- a metal stick and put this in the -- in the ground, push -- push it deep inside, and then retrieve it, smell the tip of it, and if it smells rotting flesh then we can have an assumption that we are indeed talking about a grave. But before being able to ascertain there is a grave, we must at least show that there are two different body parts so that it is not an individual grave. So in this instance we opened an area approximately 2 by 2 metres, and here we exposed a total of six bodies, which is in fact the first slice of a larger grave. This -- this one contained a total of 33 bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 6.4 has on it six different yellow arrows. Do those arrows -- in fact, it's a bit difficult to make out -- depict the six different bodies you referred to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's only to individualise them, because on such graves the bodies look more like junk. It's hard to recognise sometimes what part of the body it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Moving on to Prosecution Exhibit 6.5. Did you identify other grave sites in the immediate vicinity of the -- of both the execution site that you discussed earlier, as well as the mass grave site you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the same area is another -- another area of mass graves to be found. This photograph dated 13 July shows both, again, the execution site and the mass grave area that we just discussed. And approximately 300 metres more south is another meadow and also nearby the -- the river a mass grave site was created there.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 6.6, were you also able to verify through aerial imagery that this particular location had been disturbed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. A comparison of imagery of before and after, after let's say July 5 and July 27, shows that in between the two dates suspect sites had appeared, and the exhumation of this area was conducted, I think it was -- it was in 1999, yes, I'm sure. It was 1999. Sixty-four bodies were recovered in this entire area. The exhumation reports I think are introduced in -- it is worth noticing that in some of them -- in one of them people were apparently shot in the grave. Bullets were found embedded at the bottom of the grave. In anticipation to questions by the Defence, I would like to make a -- another comment on both the execution site and the two mass grave sites, that is, that so far the only connection that we can make among these sites are the geographical proximity. We would not in any case say that these -- the bodies found in these graves are the bodies from that execution sites -- site. It only sounds logical, but we cannot prove it because we could not conduct shell casing and analysis and comparison in that situation for the reason that due to the way this execution was committed shell casings did not mix together with the bodies. Also we have on photograph no trace of heavy equipment being used to scoop the bodies off the ground on the meadow, so the bodies were probably picked by hand and then dropped inside the mass graves. So no shell casings could be -- could be used in fact to make connections. Not only this, is that the comparisons we do are based on shell casing analysis, and in 1999 there was no more shell casings to collect along the side of this road because very strangely in 1996 at the time there was not one dollar available in this area. There was an impressive cleaning up of the road between Nova Kasaba and the intersection of Konjevic Polje with new crash barriers installed, also new gravel put alongside of the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm going to have to object to the narrative of this witness. He's not answering any questions posed by the Prosecution. He's just going on in his own narrative form. And I'd like to ask that the Court direct the Prosecution to please keep it to question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I think this is just the question I would like to ask: Witness, we understand that you are eager to give your evidence, but the whole proceeding is a question-answer orientated procedure. If the Prosecution needs more information, she probably could ask you to give your answer. Well, Ms. De la Torre, I think you have to lead the witness step by step, rather than let him answer any question that the Defence counsel did not ask yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, we have a brief video labelled "Prosecution Exhibit 10.10" which depicts area entire area of Nova Kasaba that you have been testifying concerning the football field as well as other surrounding sites. If we could play that now.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. The aim of this video again is not so good. It's just to indicate how the terrain looks like and give a -- give a feeling of the distances. Here turning towards the left is the direction of Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the big hill we always refer to -- Konjevic Polje. Sorry. This is the big hill we always refer to. And this is now the access road that goes towards Nova Kasaba, with the river at the right. The loss of quality is too big. Here is the meadow we were showing before. Here is the second mass grave area we -- we already discussed. And here is now the football field. So the aim of this video was just to show how the things are -- are in relation each with another in terms -- in geographical terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, moving on to Prosecution Exhibit 7.1, were you able to identify another execution site in this immediate vicinity?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- well, Ms. De la Torre, if you finished a section of the questions, could we have a break here?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. De la Torre, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I saw you were standing, so you might have some procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, moving from the execution site that you had identified as Nova Kasaba, were you subsequently able to identify a nearby location in a place named Cerska?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court how it was that you first identified this particular location as a potential crime scene?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I personally interviewed a witness - that was during the summer 1995 - who declared that he was on that hill above Konjevic Polje overlooking the asphalt road, trying to find a good time to attempt to cross that road. He was with a little group of men. And at one point he sees three buses who are quitting the asphalt road coming from Konjevic Polje towards Nova Kasaba, turning right, and entering the so-called valley of Cerska. That is a narrow valley just in front of the hill at Konjevic Polje. This -- these three buses were followed by an APC, an armoured personnel carrier, and then he lose these vehicles from site once they have entered the valley. He then notices that an excavator is following the same direction and after losing this one from sight he hears intense shooting coming from the valley. Sometime later, approximately half an hour, he notices these buses coming out of a valley, this time empty. The first time he noticed that there were people inside he could not -- he was not able to see if it was men or women, only people. And sometime later also he sees the excavator quitting this valley.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'm really sorry, Your Honour. But he refers to "he says" all the way through the transcript. We have no idea to authenticate this if he's talking about a witness, if he's talking about an investigator. Could we just identify who it is that he's quoting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think he said that it's a witness, but -- but Prosecutor might ask some questions to help us to have some clarification of that issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, the information you just provided to the Court, was all of that obtained during the course of your interview with this particular witness?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll just repeat what I said. I started by saying that I had interviewed a witness during the summer 1995. I interviewed him personally during the summer 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Did you receive information from any other witnesses that corroborated this particular witness's account regarding the incident you just described?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was together, as I said, with a little group of men. And during that night they managed to cross the asphalt road. They penetrated the valley. At one point a -- they penetrated the valley. They stayed in that valley during -- approximately one week. After that week, they went back. They didn't know where to go. They decided to go back towards Srebrenica. And on the way back, they noticed at one point a disgusting stench. They also noticed that on the part of a hill there was soil that had been removed, and they draw the conclusion that they probably just came across a mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Were you able to take the information that you had been given and identify a location that matched that particular description?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Based on that information, once we could access the territory, that is, in 1996, we tried to locate a possible mass grave in that area. We had no aerial imagery available of it, and we probed various areas that we considered as suspect, initially with negative results. So we filmed with a video camera the entire valley, and another investigator presented that film to this -- the three men who were together with that witness, and one of them pointed on one part of a video an area, saying that it was very nearby that spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Based upon that information, were you able personally to go out and locate this particular site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of the following mission that was built based on this information we obtained, we returned to the Cerska Valley and precisely at the area that had been indicated by that man to my colleague we started a dig and probed this area with positive results.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning your attention to Prosecution Exhibit 7.1, could you describe this location to the Court and how it corresponded to the information obtained from the witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this photograph shows the -- the execution site and the burial site inside the valley of Cerska. The photograph is taken in the direction when leaving the valley of Cerska. These vehicles are parked in a way that they would exit the valley of Cerska here. The dark side at the left of the photograph is an area which is not so clear on this picture because now it's very dark here, which is the -- the slope from which an excavator probably took soil and then covered the bodies which were only dropped at the edge of this slope. And on the left side of the road a number of shell casings were found.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Moving to Prosecution Exhibit 7.2, Mr. Ruez, we have a video of this particular location. If we could play that now and you could point out for the Court any areas of significance in the video.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the intersection of Konjevic Polje, to the left direction Bratunac. This is the hill we always referred to as the Konjevic Polje hill. This is looking towards Bratunac. Here the helicopter flies towards Konjevic Polje -- towards Nova Kasaba, sorry. This is the road that leads towards Nova Kasaba. At one point that road will turn right, just here. The witness was on the hill to the left. And then this road turns right inside the valley. On the first portion one can see what is happening on this part of the terrain when being on the hill, but very quickly -- this piece of video -- yeah, now the helicopter is going to fly inside the valley of Cerska. This is the valley, totally inhabited valley. So we arrived here. There is another turn. And here no one could see what is happening in this area when on the -- on the hill. Now it's getting deep inside the valley. Two steep hills on both sides. This is still the dirt road that goes up to the top of this valley. And here is a zoom-in where the execution area is and the burial area. The asphalt road is -- the dirt road is just underneath the line of trees. Oh, sorry, it's not the first zooming. It was the second one. There's a right turn towards the village of Macesi, and then it continues a little bit, and here is the very precise area. Now is the same area filmed from the ground. Here is the part of the hill where obviously an excavator took that soil and dug that soil on the area to the left, covering bodies which are buried under this slope. This marks the beginning of the area we will probe. We will probe this area up to the tree, which is a bit further up. This is the length of the grave. So here is the first probe, a jacket, a skull. On the right there is a colleague collecting and marking the locations of shell casings. So obviously those who were shooting was -- were on this side of the path, and their victims were just on opposite side and they fell on the slope after having been shot. This is the second probe with feet and legs coming out of the ground where we dug. And this is a third probe that exposes a skull, the top of the skull. So this is again an aerial view to show this time not the entrance but the exit way of the valley. This is the length of the valley, the steep hill -- the big hill at the -- at the end of the landscape is the hill of Konjevic Polje. So the buses drove approximately 2 kilometres inside this valley to bring the -- the victims.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, looking at Prosecution Exhibit 7.3, were you ultimately able to obtain aerial imagery that also corresponded to the particular site here at Cerska?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Following that discovery, we requested confirmation of a date of creation of this site. Following our request, we received two photographs, one dated July 5 that shows the area where we probed without any obvious disturbance there, and the same area dated 27 July 1995, that shows the two disturbances, one at the left that corresponds to the grave area and one to the right of the dirt road that corresponds to the piece of slope that has been taken by the excavator to cover these bodies. Ultimately, once the excavation was covered on that spot, 150 bodies were exhumed. But Mr. Manning will come and give all details about the findings from the grave sites and the connections that are made based on these findings.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Moving on from the site at Cerska, Mr. Ruez, we'll show you Prosecution Exhibit 8.1, which is the intersection at Konjevic Polje. Going back to this particular location, can you explain to the Court what is the significance of Konjevic Polje and its location there.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So this photograph is taken from the hill but just at the bottom of the hill that overlooks the area. This is the direction north, that is, the asphalt road that goes towards Zvornik. To the right is the direction of Bratunac and to the left is the direction of Nova Kasaba. So this is also a surrender spot and also a spot from which -- from where witnesses -- one witness, who is identified but I don't know if I can give his name. I don't know if he was a protected witness or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: I would prefer that you not at this point.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. So this -- on this photograph one can see the direction of -- where it is marked "Jadar River," in fact, the Jadar River is at the left of the picture and continues inside the valley and reaches the Drina River. At one point it become it is Drinjaca River when arriving inside this canyon. One man who tried to cross this asphalt road, the witness who I was just referring to previously who I don't identify yet, tried to cross here but was spotted and arrested.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: There is in the centre of this particular exhibit, Mr. Ruez, a yellow arrow pointing to what appears to be a white house. What is the significance of that particular location?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a hangar, in fact, a warehouse we call it, which is demolished since then, which is in fact a detention site for prisoners who were captured in this vicinity. They were first taken to a vicinity that we will show on the next exhibits. And ultimately these people were put in this warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 8.2, can you describe for the Court the other detention facilities and military facilities in that immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When going from the intersection of Konjevic Polje towards Bratunac, approximately 500 metres to the east is located the compound of the 5th Engineer Regiment, which is the -- Engineer Unit, sorry, which is a of the Drina Corps. The witness I was referring to once got -- once he got arrested was first taken to this building. He didn't step inside. He just was stopped at the -- taken to the guardhouse, that is, the little building just at the entrance. And from there he was taken to another building that is very nearby this facility, some 100 metres away from it, and that is the Exhibit 8.3.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at 8.3, what is depicted on that particular exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are two houses in the -- in the shape they were in April 1996. They were in that same shape in summer 1995. You are -- also can see in between two vehicles which are bridge trucks. The reason why I point these is that later you will be shown aerial imagery where these trucks are also visible on it, and this enables you to compare how an object looks on the ground versus how it looks when it appears on aerial imagery. But the reason why this image is on the screen is because the house to the right is a house where with -- where this prisoner was taken to and it was the communication room of the 5th Engineer Unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Going back to Prosecution Exhibit 8.1. You indicated that this particular individual was apprehended while trying to cross the asphalt road. Once he was taken into custody as a prisoner, can you describe the different facilities and the order in which he was held there in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 5th Engineer Unit being, as I said, about 500 metres to the right of this photograph, direction Bratunac, that prisoner was then taken from the communication house to the hangar, which is marked with the yellow arrow right in the middle of the photograph. He was there together with a group of 15 others. And after some time, a bus came. They were taken onboard of a bus and driven towards the Jadar River, where the arrow is pointing towards the top of this picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: What happened once these 16 prisoners arrived at the Jadar River?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were instructed to step out of the bus. They went down a steep slope towards the river bank of the Jadar River, and one soldier was standing behind them and opened fire on them. One bullet went through the hip of our witness, who fell in the water and got out of it sometime later. I think let his body float on it for a -- for a short distance and ultimately managed to reach Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Based upon the information received from this witness, did you accompany him in an attempt to locate the execution site that he had referred to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We -- we brought him there. I could have added a series of pictures to show you the area, but it is a bit useless for the reason that no evidence could be collected from such a site. The river is much more strong during -- during the beginning of the year probably because the water line was visible on the trees some 1 metre higher than the level of the river was when we went there. A lot of trash was hanging on the branches of -- of the lower branches of the trees, showing that at one point between the time we arrived there and the time the events happened the river had washed away everything what was there. So we made an attempt to try to find shell casings in that place, but it was useless. This is a witness we can only believe on -- on -- based on his good faith, I could say.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 8.4. Were you subsequently able to identify other crime scenes in this particular area of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did -- we made a request for imagery, specifically for this area in order to try to identify exhumation sites though they would be disconnected from crime scenes for which we would have witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: There were several -- several suspect sites in this area. We did probe all of them. Not all of them had successful results, but two of them indeed had. And on this photograph dated 14 August, you have at the right of this photograph again the hill overlooking Konjevic Polje. At the bottom of the picture, turning to the left of the picture is the dirt road that goes towards the valley of Cerska and at the bottom of the picture is the road that goes towards Nova Kasaba. Behind a tree line is a suspect site that we named KP1, which indeed is a mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 8.5, does this photograph depict, albeit in colour, the site that you mentioned as KP1?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Here we are looking at the site from another angle. Now Konjevic Polje is at the bottom left of the picture, and the road is going towards Nova Kasaba. So this is the road that was taken by the column of trucks deporting the population. And the way this grave is set is obviously to hide it from the view of the people who are travelling from the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 8.6, can you describe for the Court what was found at the site labelled "KP1".

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went there to probe the site once we did assess this imagery. I think it was in 1998, but I cannot ascertain really that date. This was the result of a probe we did there that enabled us to uncover a skull. The full exhumation of that site led to the discovery of nine bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 8.7.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is also the result of a probe we did on another suspect area in the vicinity of Konjevic Polje. This is about 3 kilometres towards the -- the east, so towards Bratunac. It was a suspect area that we probed and then exhumed. Only three bodies were discovered in that disturbed area.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Was that site labelled "KP2"?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, looking at Prosecution Exhibit 8.8, you mentioned earlier the mobile brigade trucks that were present outside the communications house of the 5th Engineers. Were you able to obtain aerial imagery that detailed the presence of digging equipment in this particular area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We -- we did access such material. So on this -- on this photograph, one can see in the middle of the picture the compound of -- of the school, that is, the -- the 5th Engineer Unit headquarters. And in the box labelled "A," you have the two houses, which we saw on the previous exhibit. And also, behind these houses you can see bridge trucks. We have -- we have a better enlargement of this. There is no need to enlarge on these ones because we have below-ups that follow. So this is a photo dated 27 July 1995. I said the bridge trucks in the box labelled "A" are there, and in the box labelled "B," there is also some equipment. We then have the next exhibit, which is 8.9, which is the blow-up of the -- the box labelled "A."

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: When you say, Mr. Ruez, "mobile bridge trucks," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the -- these are truck that is can unfold and that creates a bridge. These are pieces of equipment that were not used at all at the time of the events. They were just sitting there. They were still there in 1996. So they are out of the scope of the investigation. It is only to enable to -- to educate all of us on how to compare on object seen from the air and an object seen from the ground, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the interest of comparing the dates is to show that there is equipment present in this compound that can be used to dig holes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
