utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 8.10. This is a photograph, again depicting the mobile brigade trucks, this time dated July 27th, 1995. In particular of interest, Mr. Ruez, there is another vehicle that's identified as a front loader.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: What is a front loader?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A front loader is a machine that has a bucket in front of it and that is used to -- to move soil from one place to another.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 8.11, dated again the 5th of July, 1995, can you explain what this particular photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the area that was labelled "B." And it shows indeed a group of houses. And on this photograph, the presence dated July 5 of only a tractor and a trailer.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Could you compare that photograph with Prosecution Exhibit 8.12, dated 27 July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So on this photograph dated indeed 27 July, in addition to the tractor and the trailer that was already present here July -- on July 5, in addition now one can see that there is one truck -- two trucks, sorry, and one additional front loader.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, as an investigator, does the presence of this -- the digging equipment that you have identified corroborate the witness accounts that you obtained concerning the activity that had occurred in this particular area during these particular dates?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, since many of them talk about this equipment, that they see moving along the road, and mainly it indicates that there was a need for bringing such equipment in that area between the July 5 and July 27. It would be my personal conclusion to connect this arrival with the events.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I would like to just voice a running objection. I don't want to interrupt the proceedings any longer. But my running objection is that every time the witness brings up some summary of witnesses that he's spoken before or evidence of someone he's spoken to before, I object that there is no authentication or reliability there. And if he would just let us know whether the witness will be present in the courtroom to testify or not, I'll know whether the objection is useful or not. But if we knew whether the witness is coming, I would have no objection. If the witness is someone that is not coming and we don't have any witness statements on, then I must -- we'll have what we call in our system a "running objection" so that I don't have to interrupt the proceedings any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh, thank you very much. I think it's a good point. I believe that the Prosecutor should indicate it, that whether this information mentioned by the witness will be present and give evidence at a later stage or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we understand that the testimony of this witness needs corroborations.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: The witness is likely not aware of whether or not the Prosecution intends to call particular witnesses. However, we do have a list, which obviously the Defence has as well, that identifies each of these witnesses and the survivors. I can by number rather than by name indicate that at the beginning in order to try and assist the Defence in identifying from the list that they already have which individual we -- we're referring to, if that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour. I would also like, since he is a -- was an employee of the OTP and probably has access to that kind of confidential information, we don't need to know the name of the witness, just whether we will be able to cross-examine them or not. So it's really an identify -- identification of whether the witness will appear, not who it is, because I might be able to figure that out through the reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour. That's exactly what I wanted to bring out, because at some points it's very unclear whether the gentleman is referring to witnesses who will appear or witnesses that he's read their statements or perhaps even spoke with but won't be appearing at trial. So and the Prosecution is in the best position to at least guide us in that. So if she could merely state that this witness will be testifying, so we know, and then Mr. Ruez can continue with his testimony, as he has been. And I would appreciate if he could keep his conclusions to himself. I understand he wishes to share with us his knowledge. He will have plenty of opportunity during cross-examination to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. We will do according to both party agrees. Maybe you could indicate the number of that witness to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And just going back for clarification, the witness that Mr. Ruez discussed as having survived being shot and falling in the Jadar River is number 59, Witness P175. And the witness he referred to who described the incidents at the Cerska Valley is number 72, Witness P109, both of whom are on the Prosecution witness list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, moving on from the area of Konjevic Polje over to the area of Sandici and Kravica, I'll turn your attention to Prosecution Exhibit 9.1. You had indicated yesterday that the Sandici meadow, that particular area, was one of two main collection points for Muslims who decided to surrender throughout the day and come down from the hills after having been trapped behind the road. Can you describe the route, using Prosecution Exhibit 9.1, that those individuals would take once they made the decision to go ahead and surrender?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So at the top of the picture would be in fact the top of the hill that is at the left side of the road that goes from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje. And when people go down that slope, they are funneled by the terrain. So one main direction that people would take is to go down by the way that is marked with the yellow dot. Then as I said, at one point they leave the dirt road, they leave a track of belongings on the meadow in front of that destroyed house, and then they get assembled on this meadow. But there are also other meadows around there, one being on the top at the right of this picture, which is the meadow of Lolici. It is another natural orientation for people who would come down that hill, and from there later on also people were taken by foot towards the meadow of Sandici. The meadow of Sandici is the main regroupment spot for the prisoners who surrender in this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And looking at Prosecution Exhibit 9.2, Mr. Ruez, does aerial imagery indeed confirm the witness accounts of having surrendered and being collected there on -- on Sandici meadow? Sorry, going back to 9.1 -- sorry, it is 9.2.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a -- a blow-up of the previous one? Yes. Corroboration of witness testimonies, yes, there are several of them. Some are not even visible clearly here, but they are -- they can be seen on other pieces of footage. We have a -- we have the photograph showing these prisoners on the spot. I don't see very well what is the question about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: In addition to the aerial images that depict prisoners being held on the field, is there videotape that exists that also corroborates the witness's account of having surrendered and been collected on Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We also have video evidence of that. On one we can see one of the witnesses who was on this meadow, but he was a witness who was not later executed because he was a young boy who managed to get on-board of a bus and he can be seen on the video. But the other survivors we have on this spot, they don't appear on any other footages. But they gave details, for example, the presence of these destroyed houses. It's fixed buildings, so one could think that people knew this area from before, so it's not really relevant. But they describe that there was a tank close to that group. They describe at one point the murder of one individual nearby that tank. One can see on this photograph that just nearby this large group of prisoners is an unidentified vehicle. It seems to be a large one. I would not say it's a tank because it's an unidentified vehicle. But we can also see large tracks going from the asphalt road towards this vehicle. Is this the tank this witness referred about, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 9.3. It appears to be a colour photograph of the exact same location that was depicted in the aerial image 9.2. Have you visited this site, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, several times. The interest of this picture is just to enable you to transpose yourself from a black-and-white aerial imagery to what the terrain really looks like, so by using again an aerial imagery but from a helicopter and in colour. And again, here the dot shows the precise path the people took before being assembled on the spot. We can say it is the precise path because we have video shot at the time of the events, and also once we went there we could see a very precise trail of belongings that the people abandoned when they were reaching the two storage -- destroyed house.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: During the course of your investigation, Mr. Ruez, were you able to ascertain whether or not General Mladic visited this site and addressed the prisoners as they were being held on the meadow?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not something that I could ascertain, but this is what the witnesses report. They say that indeed at one point of the day, probably around noon, General Mladic arrived with a crew of people and he also -- he addressed the crowd, gave some promises about future exchange, and then left the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Do those accounts of General Mladic addressing the prisoners on Sandici meadow correspond to the accounts of General Mladic having made the same address on the Nova Kasaba football field?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it seems that that day, July 13, General Mladic was visiting several sites where prisoners were kept, and more or less in the same pattern gave a speech to his people, gave some security guarantees, and then left. It happened in Bratunac in one hangar. It happened at the Sandici meadow, and it happened also at the Nova Kasaba football field.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 9.4. You had indicated there was a trail of belongings behind this house. When was it, do you recall, that you first were able to visit and physically examine this particular site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in April 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And upon that inspection, were you able yourself to identify a trail of belongings that had been left on that field?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is one picture that shows that trail, when on the top of the balcony of that house and looking down it's even more obvious. But the ground is scattered with various personal items, including plastics of UNHCR and various items, personal belongings. And the meadow also was covered with those, including some pieces of ID that we have collected and turned into evidence, a homemade stretcher found on the ground, items like this that were just left over from the prisoners when they were taken away from this site.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 9.5, Mr. Ruez, can you explain the significance of the location that you have marked as the Kravica warehouse vis-a-vis the Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph is taken when standing behind the two-storey destroyed house and looking in the direction towards Bratunac. Approximately 800 metres in that direction is a warehouse complex, I recall the Kravica warehouse complex. The village of Kravica being a few hundred metres more in the direction west.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 10.1, Mr. Ruez, it appears to be a colour photograph of a warehouse. Is this the warehouse that you referred to as the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: When did you first identify the Kravica warehouse as a potential crime scene?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: First it -- it happened in two stages. The first stage was the interview of -- of an individual that we conducted in, I think, summer 1995, who was our first survivor for the Kravica warehouse. Based on his information -- he was kept in the right part of the warehouse, which is the west part, so the right of this photograph. And based on his information we made a first check of this warehouse in January 1996. But it was a very short visit. In fact, the -- the entire building was processed for forensic analysis in June 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the sake of the record and Defence counsel, there are three Kravica warehouse survivors to whom Mr. Ruez will be referring. They are number 41, witness P193; number 62, witness P106; and number 63, witness P107, all of whom are on the Prosecution witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 10.2, Mr. Ruez, this appears to be an aerial image dated 13 July. Can you explain to the Court what it is about this particular image that corresponds to the witness statements of the survivors at the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That photograph is dated 13 July 1995, 1400 hours, and it shows the presence of two buses in -- in that compound of the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: What is -- I'm sorry. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The importance of this, in terms of corroboration of witness testimony, is that one of these witnesses you mentioned -- survivors you mentioned was in the first group that was taken from the Sandici meadow towards this warehouse, and they were taken on-board of buses. They drove towards direction Bratunac but they stopped when reaching this compound. They turned right, which is the -- to reach the entrance of this compound, and then parked -- his bus was parked just in front of the broad opening. So obviously the bus in which this person was is the bus that -- there is a second one when going from left to right. The reason to know that also is that this bus will stay here, probably because it suffered some damage during what happened there. The witness remembers having heard a very sharp noise of air being expulsed from something. So it's probably that the tyre of this bus was hit at one point, and we have imagery showing this bus staying there.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 10.3. This appears to be a panorama of the same building. Can you explain when this particular photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in wintertime. It's the -- it's the first pictures that we took of the warehouse. It's in January 1996. It's the -- the closest timing possible with the date of the events.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: On this particular image, Mr. Ruez, can you explain what elements are depicted that correspond to the witness accounts of what occurred in the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The building has to be looked as two -- two elements, because two groups of prisoners were taken -- taken separately inside this building. The first group, as I said, arrived there by bus and they were taken into the east part, which on this picture is at the left of the picture. They were occupying the -- the inside of the warehouse, just where the -- the wall is blocking the exit. So in front of these left openings there was no prisoners. So prisoners were pushed in the left part of this -- of this -- of the building. So not the entire surface of the left part of the building was -- was filled with the prisoners. The right part of the building is a different situation. A large group of prisoners from the Sandici meadow were made to walk towards Bratunac, and in fact arriving at the Kravica warehouse they entered this right part of the warehouse, which is at the west, through these doors, through the door which is here now broken but at the time it was not in that -- broken like this. And this right part of the warehouse was completely filled with prisoners, according to their accounts.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Did you receive information from the survivors of the Kravica warehouse that you were able to subsequently corroborate once you were able to visit the scene?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I was in another thought. Could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Sure. Did you receive -- or based on the interviews that you conducted with the Kravica warehouse survivors, did you obtain information that you were able to subsequently corroborate once you were able to inspect the site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court the detail that was provided to you from the survivors that you were able to corroborate once you arrived on the scene.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two series of details. One -- some can some from observations that are made on the buildings and inside the buildings, and others are elements which are coming from the exhumation of the mass grave where these prisoners have then been buried. But together with them were also buried elements which were to be found inside the warehouse and that were described by -- by one of the survivors. So starting with the building, one -- one element that cannot be seen on the picture is that the person said having survived thanks to the fact that he could find a -- there was a little, he says, guardhouse inside this right part of the warehouse and he managed to crawl inside. That protected him from injury. When we arrived there the first time, I in fact thought that we were in the wrong place because there was no guardhouse inside the building. In reality, it was such a short visit that we could not really do what we were supposed to do there. And we found traces on the wall that showed that indeed there had been a guardhouse in that building but this guardhouse has been destroyed at the same time the bodies were taken away, and we have, I think, photographs -- or at least on the film we can make stops where I will be able to show you where this, in brackets, guardhouse was located.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Beginning with what occurred there at the Kravica warehouse, what did the survivors indicate happened once they arrived?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- apparently the reconstruction of the events would be that the killing happened in the -- in two phases. Phase one was the killing of the people who were in the west part of the warehouse, and then the execution switched on the other part of the warehouse. According to the witness who was detained in the west part, as soon as he was entering -- he entered that warehouse that was already packed with people, there was fire getting -- fire was opened from all the openings of this building. Grenades were thrown inside, and this happened in various ways. I'm not going to describe the entire statement of these people, since you already have them and we'll hear it again from -- from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Before we move on from this particular exhibit, 10.3, Mr. Ruez, could you explain the significance of the markings that are on the wall surrounding the second window from the right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Various things in terms of markings. Pockmarks are obviously the result of a shooting on this building. There is also destruction on the right part of the building. You can see a large door with a broken wall on the right and a broken upper part of a door at the top. These destructions were caused by the excavator -- I mean, front loader that entered this building after the executions to collect the bodies. These pieces of concrete were later found in the mass grave where the bodies had been buried, as well as hay that was also thrown on the bodies after the execution as well as body -- pieces of vehicle that were also inside the warehouse at the time. The blow-up on this window is of interest, to be later on compared with the live footage taken by Zoran Petrovic, when he was in company of General Borovcanin in this area and he filled this part of the warehouse with a stack of dead bodies on the ground. When one looks tentatively like we will do later on this footage, at this specific window it will be seen that there are no bullet traces on that part of the wall, versus they exist here in -- in January 1996. That's an indication that the massacre here was ongoing at the moment these live pictures were being -- were filmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Moving inside the warehouse itself, Mr. Ruez, I'll turn to Prosecution Exhibit 10.4. When you arrived on the scene in 1996, what did you discover within the warehouse that corroborated the witness account?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this photograph, this photograph depicts a blood stain at the angle of a wall to this one because it was very obvious even on a photograph. We have made available all the forensic reports about the findings on this place, so you already know that more or less every single piece of -- of whatever was on this wall ended up being human residue or pieces of hair, of skin, or blood and other things. The entire place is scattered with these things. Not necessarily as impressive as such a large stain, but a lot of residue in this place.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 10.5, can you inform the Court what this picture depicts?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a picture of the ceiling of -- of one part of the ceiling, because not the entire ceiling of this building shows these things. But these are bloodstains also on the ceiling, which is quite a high ceiling, 2 -- 3 metres high, I would assess. And this is also consistent with severed body parts from an explosion blast, grenade explosions that would -- that would throw a piece of body at that ceiling and leave a stain on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 10.6, can you explain the significance of this particular photograph and the angle from which it was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did summarise a bit the execution process that took part at the west of the warehouse. But the first group that arrived, arrived by bus and was put in the east part, and apparently since those were kept in that part were being told that during all this intense shooting that in fact they were under attack from the column from the hills, it seems to indicate that there were probably not enough men available to do the two killings in one, so they first did one part and then they switched on the other part. The window that can be seen at the right of this -- of the building, that is, the back of a building, is the window from which -- through which one of our survivors jumped through. Then he lied in the cornfield that is behind here. The corn is -- is cut.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Prosecution Exhibit 10.7, which is a close-up of the particular window.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a window at the east part of the warehouse, when looking at the warehouse from the asphalt road. According to the -- to the victims, people tried in any way to flee this place, so some were jumping out of the windows. And here we have one of these windows and we have a shoe trace just above the first bullet hole that is underneath. When we blow up the shoe trace we can see that it is the reverse of a shoe. It is not the shoe of someone who is climbing through this window but it is the shoe of someone who -- the shoe print of someone who is trying to get out of this window.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Looking at Exhibit 10.8, is that in fact a close-up of the shoe print you were referring?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: And as you indicated, these shoe prints, it's a bit difficult to tell on this particular photograph, is facing towards the ground?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the ground. This is the shoe print of someone who is getting out of the window and trying to get out of this building.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time we have a videotape that was taken depicting the crime scene at Kravica warehouse labelled "Prosecution Exhibit 10.9." I believe it's -- might be right at about ten minutes, so we can either start that now or defer that until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's watch the video today. And you may ask some questions concerning with the video next Monday.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So this is Sandici, the two-storey destroyed house. Here is the Sandici meadow, with the corn at the left. Then the asphalt road. So here it is filming towards the direction of Bratunac, so Kravica. And to indicate the distance, here there will be a zoom-in. And just underneath the tree line at the end will be the Kravica warehouse. The approximate distance, I would say 800 metres. So this is a view from above. Unfortunately, we have again the problem of the quality. This is the entire warehouse complex. Here the right door had been repaired. This was filmed in 1999, and the right part of the door has been repaired. It's continuing. Could we cut the sound? This video -- this piece of video here was filmed by a colleague named Peter Nicholson in 1996, April 1996. And the outside impacts are obviously due to a fact that people were running out of this, as we can see later on in the live video. The bodies are outside the warehouse for some of them. This is -- these are other traces of the so-called guardhouse inside, and at the bottom there are also some specific tiles that mark the perimeter of this former guardhouse. This is the shape of the inside walls. I also mentioned that beside the pieces that have been collected by the ICTY experts who were doing forensic in this building, the building has never been cleaned from 1995 through to 1999. I don't even know if it is done yet. Some of these black traces at the bottom are explosive residues. What we just saw was the east part -- sorry, the west part. And here is then the east part. So where these large openings are, there were no prisoners behind. But prisoners were here at the left. So this is the area where there was no one, in front of the openings. And all this area here, the prisoners were sitting. This part of the warehouse had not been fully processed by the forensic people, but I went personally to collect one blood trace in 1998. We presented it to the lab, and it was told to be human blood. Here in 1996 there is a live grenade that had been forgotten at the edge of the road. It might be there for any other reasons. I would not say that it's July 1995. This is the result of a -- of a dig that we did on a little area of trash. And going through that trash, we found shell casings, a few cover pages of ID documents, and a collection of bones. We were together with Dr. Bill Haglund who gave us an indication that these bones for most of them were human bones. There were a few animal bones also with it. There is also fake teeth at the left. This is the back of the warehouse, where also shell casings were found. But here unfortunately there is no straight zoom on it. The pieces that have been selected for this footage is only showing grenade handles. And these grenade handles were found just underneath that window and there were a few more grenade handles found underneath the following window.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LA TORRE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that concludes the video of this particular scene video. We do have another clip of video and a few more things to cover with regard to Kravica warehouse, if you'd like me to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we have to stop at this moment. Next Monday we'll have the afternoon session, which will start at 2.15 in the same courtroom. We are adjourned now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 1.45 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of May, 2003, at 2.15 p.m.
